title: The Airlock
style_tags: Star Trek cinematic 3D animation, semi-realistic Pixar-quality characters, detailed Starfleet uniforms with fabric texture, glowing LCARS console panels, dramatic sci-fi lighting with lens flares, deep space backgrounds with nebulae and stars, cinematic depth of field, volumetric light from viewscreens

characters.name: Kirk
characters.character_description: semi-realistic Pixar 3D Captain James T. Kirk, athletic build, light brown hair swept to side, strong jaw, confident commanding expression, gold-yellow TOS Starfleet command tunic with delta badge, upper body portrait
characters.status: Physically overrode Worf at the emergency release panel. Pulled the lever. Found the airlock completely empty — no Chekov, only frost boot prints tracking to the sealed outer door. Standing at the threshold, unable to explain what he is looking at.

relationships.Worf: ally under pressure — but something is wrong
relationships.Chekov: crew member he refused to abandon

characters.name: Worf
characters.character_description: semi-realistic Pixar 3D Commander Worf, imposing Klingon-Human, prominent forehead ridges, dark skin, fierce disciplined expression, TNG Starfleet command red uniform with lieutenant commander pips, broad shoulders, intense dark eyes
characters.status: Blocked Kirk's path to the emergency release. Gave his final warning — 'Command will arrest us both.' Stepped aside when Kirk said 'Move. Worf.' Witnessed the empty airlock alongside Kirk. Now both of them have no explanation.

characters.name: Chekov
characters.character_description: semi-realistic Pixar 3D Ensign Pavel Chekov, young face, distinctive bowl-cut dark hair, wide fearful eyes, pale skin, TOS gold Starfleet uniform, panicked desperate expression
characters.status: VANISHED. Airlock was empty when Kirk opened the door. Only frost boot prints remain on the grated floor, tracking toward the sealed outer door — which was never opened. No body, no explanation.

relationships.Kirk: trusts captain completely — begged for help

active_loops: major: Who is the real enemy agent on the Enterprise?
major: How did Chekov vanish from a sealed airlock — outer door was never opened?
eternal: Kirk always fights for his crew against the system
closed_loops: minor: Is Chekov really a traitor or was he framed? — SUSPENDED: Chekov has disappeared, question cannot be answered yet

important_items: Sealed airlock door — SEALED indicator burning red
PADD with the Fleet Admiral's signed order
Chekov behind the sealed door — fate unknown
key_events: EP1: Worf executed airlock procedure on Chekov on Fleet Admiral's orders
EP1: Kirk ordered 'Cancel the procedure' — Worf refused, claimed Fleet Admiral signed personally
EP1: Kirk and Worf watched airlock seal. Kirk's fist clenched.
EP1: Kirk asked 'Worf. Who really gave you that order.' — Worf dropped his eyes and said nothing
EP2: Kirk physically moved toward emergency release panel — Worf stepped in his path
EP2: Worf's final warning: 'Captain. If you open that door — Command will arrest us both.'
EP2: Kirk: 'Move. Worf.' — Worf stepped aside
EP2: Kirk pulled the emergency release lever — SEALED became OPEN
EP2: Airlock was empty. Only frost boot prints tracking to the sealed outer door — which was never opened

episode_summaries.summary: Kirk moves on the emergency release panel. Worf steps into his path and warns him: 'Captain. If you open that door — Command will arrest us both.' Kirk says 'Move. Worf.' — and Worf steps aside. Kirk pulls the lever. The airlock opens. The chamber is completely empty. On the grated floor: frost boot prints tracking toward the sealed outer door — which was never opened.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: The airlock is empty. Chekov vanished from a sealed room. The outer door was never opened — and there is no explanation.

episode_summaries.summary: Worf leads Chekov to the airlock on Fleet Admiral's orders. Kirk commands Worf to stand down — refused. Worf claims the order was signed personally by the Fleet Admiral. Kirk and Worf watch the airlock seal. Chekov screams it's a setup from behind the glass. Kirk stares at the sealed door and asks: 'Worf. Who really gave you that order.' Worf drops his eyes. Silence.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Worf knows who really gave the order — and it wasn't the Fleet Admiral
